item.title: This Vikings QB timeline since 2023 proves Kevin O’Connell isn’t the guru everybody thought
item.description: This Vikings QB timeline since 2023 proves Kevin O’Connell isn’t the guru everybody thought originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is one of the winningest active coaches in the NFL, but his status as a quarterback whisperer is being called into question. At one point, O'Connell was considered a bright young head coach who would get the most out of any quarterback on his team. Over time, though, the Vikings still haven't solved their quarterback issues, while Minnesota's former signal-callers have thrived elsewhere. Now, with Kyler Murray the latest Vikings quarterback who isn't playing up to expectations, O'Connell's status as a quarterback guru has waned. The Vikings head coach needs to turn that around for Minnesota to compete for a Super Bowl. Here's a breakdown of every quarterback to start a game with the Vikings under O'Connell. MORE : Who needs Jonathan Taylor the most? Vikings QB timeline under Kevin O'Connell Kirk Cousins (2022-23) O'Connell inherited Cousins when he first arrived in Minnesota in 2022, and the two were a great pair. Cousins started every game for the Vikings that year, leading Minnesota to the playoffs with a 13-4 record while totaling 4,547 passing yards and 29 passing touchdowns. That season continued Cousins' strong play for the Vikings, as his numbers were similar to his seasonal production since signing with Minnesota in 2018. From a wins standpoint, though, Cousins had only won double-digit games once before and had never won more than 10 contests. In 2023, Cousins had a solid start before he tore his Achilles, which was a huge blow ahead of free agency. In 25 games with O'Connell, Cousins produced 275.12 passing yards per game with 37 passing touchdowns in total. Josh Dobbs (2023) After Cousins tore his Achilles, the Vikings traded for quarterback Josh Dobbs, who had been solid for the Arizona Cardinals in place of an injured Kyler Murray. While the Cardinals had just one win up to that point, Dobbs had 14 total touchdowns, passing and rushing, and showed enough to get a chance elsewhere. Dobbs' production slightly dipped when he began playing for the Vikings, and he was unable to fill Cousins' shoes. Dobbs started four games for Minnesota, appearing in five total contests, and had just 179 passing yards per game. In the final five games of the season, Mullens started three of them but failed to lead the team to a win in any of those starts. item.title: 4 winners and losers from the Patriots’ loss to the Packers
item.description: The New England Patriots were largely uncompetitive in a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. They have now dropped to 5-4 on the season. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 9 contest. Winners N/A Losers CB Christian Gonzalez: The Patriots’ top corner was not his usual self on Sunday. Gonzalez was on scene for several explosive plays and took fault for a miscommunication that resulted in Matthew Golden’s 5-yard touchdown. Both Golden and Christian Watson posted 80-plus yards with Gonzalez in coverage while he surrendered 187 yards on a career-high 10 receptions in total. New England’s secondary is too talented to be playing at this level in recent weeks, and that begins with Gonzalez. QB Drake Maye: There were positive moments for Maye against Green Bay, but the quarterback ultimately struggled throwing three first-half interceptions that led to an early deficit. Maye’s interceptions came when he pushed the ball down the field, which was a concern entering the week against a zone heavy Packers defense that led the league in takeaways. Offensive line: Behind their fifth different starting combination, the pressure got to Maye early on Sunday. The Packers’ pressure schemes gave New England’s front fits as Maye was sacked four times and was forced into four throwaways. In total, Maye was under pressure on over 50% of his drop backs. RG Matt Pryor was initially charted with four pressures to lead the group. Injuries: As they have all season, the injuries continued to pile up. The Patriots lost CB Carlton Davis (knee), LG Ben Brown (knee), ST Brenden Schooler (hamstring), and RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) in the loss. They did get positive news with starting left tackle Will Campbell, who would have returned in a closer game, but the roster is beaten down ahead of a trip to Germany — which could alter recovery timelines as the team departs Wednesday evening. Honorable mentions DeMario Douglas recorded his second career 100-yard game behind a beautifully-ran 36-yard corner-post route. Mack Hollins finished with three catches and a touchdown in his return. Efton Chism also found the end zone and had five catches. It was a down day for Kyle Williams, who failed to haul in a deep ball and was targeted on Maye’s second interception (which was on the quarterback). Rhamondre Stevenson’s fumble was the Patriots fourth turnover of the day. They now have a -11 turnover differential on the season. Milton Williams flashed throughout the day with three pressures and a TFL in the run game. Rookie cornerback Karon Prunty replaced an injured Carlton Davis at corner. While Prunty had an impressive gunner rep to help down a punt, the Packers immediately picked on him defensively. Packers were 4-of-5 in the red zone. The Patriots kickoff coverage continues to be shaky as they allowed a 48-yard return. Punter Mitch Wishnowsky continues to punt well and recorded four i20s.

item.title: Dion Dublin backs Michael Carrick for more time and tells Manchester United players to 'point fingers' at each other after chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa
item.description: Manchester United v Aston Villa FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Former Manchester United and Aston Villa striker Dion Dublin has urged Old Trafford chiefs to stick with under-fire manager Michael Carrick following Sunday's thrilling 4-4 Premier League stalemate. Despite twice overturning two-goal deficits to salvage a dramatic stoppage-time point at home, the Red Devils remain inside the relegation zone. Stoppage-time rescue salvages home point Dublin insists United's squad must take collective responsibility rather than blaming their manager after shipping 30 goals across all competitions this term , more than any side in Europe's top five leagues. Alysson and Nicolas Jackson scored early before Bruno Fernandes' penalty and former Villa midfielder Youri Tielemans made it 2-2 at half-time. After John McGinn's spot-kick and Leon Goretzka restored Villa's two-goal cushion, Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a stoppage-time point . item.description: Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula. © IMAGN The All-American 2026 WTA Finals Group 1 match between Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula lasted two hours and 39 minutes on Sunday in Indian Wells. Gauff won the match in three sets, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-2. During the match, Gauff excelled in covering the court, making it physically exhausting for Pegula to keep up with the two-time Grand Slam champion. In the post-match conference, Pegula said Gauff’s movement made it difficult for her. This was also why Pegula looked pretty exhausted in the third set. “It’s tough when a match gets really physical against Coco; to be honest, it’s probably not in my favor,” Pegula told reporters as seen in Christian Court’s X. “I think the first two sets especially were super physical, and I just had a little lull at the beginning of the third, which was unfortunate, like that first game… I thought her movement, I mean, I say this every time, but is the best on tour. Like, it’s insane, her court coverage. I felt like I was coming into the net, sticking volleys, and I’m like ready to walk, turn around, and she’s, even if I won the point, she was still there.” Pegula also acknowledged the mistakes she made in the first set, including missed “volleys, overheads and short balls.” Pegula had a break opportunity in the ninth game of the opening set, but she failed to execute. In the end, Gauff held her serve and went on to break the fellow American in the very next game to win the first set. Pegula and Gauff’s match was one of two opening-day matches in Indian Wells on Sunday. The other match saw Linda Noskova beating Elena Rybakina’s replacement, Marta Kostyuk, in straight sets. Gauff herself acknowledged how much running the match required. She joked that her shoes were badly worn out, with pieces of rubber left on the court. “But I also had to run a lot,” Gauff said. “My shoes are pretty torn up now. Some of my shoes… like somewhere on the court there. So I’m gonna have to change shoes tomorrow.” Gauff also praised Pegula’s ball striking. “Jess is an incredible player. We always go back and forth,” Gauff said of Pegula via Yahoo Sports. “She does really great ball striking; she keeps the ball low when she’s really aggressive. So I think today the key was just trying to be aggressive.” Gauff, who is seeking to win her second WTA Finals title, will face Linda Noskova in her next game. Meanwhile, Pegula will face Kostyuk in the other Group 1 match. item.title: Alycia Baumgardner eases past Elif Nur Turhan as Caroline Dubois hype intensifies
item.description: Alycia Baumgardner moved a step closer to a fight with Caroline Dubois on Sunday, dominating Elif Nur Turhan to become IBF lightweight champion. Baumgardner was undisputed at super-featherweight before venturing up to her new division, where all three judges gave her all 10 rounds against Nur Turhan. With that, Nur Turhan lost her IBF title and unbeaten record, while Baumgardner closed in on a unification fight with Britain’s Dubois . Dubois even spoke to her American rival from ringside after the main event had finished, in a reversal of a scene from August – when Baumgardner did the same following Dubois’s win over Amelia Moore. While Dubois used her time on the microphone on Sunday to call for a fight with Baumgardner, 32, the Britain must first beat Stephanie Han in February. In that fight, Dubois, 25, will put her WBC and WBO titles on the line, while Han’s WBA strap will be up for grabs. Both fighters will enter that bout unbeaten. Baumgardner trading words with Caroline Dubois in August (Getty) Also on Sunday’s card in Arlington, Texas, Ramla Ali beat Mikiah Krips by split decision to pick up the vacant IBF and WBO belts at super-bantamweight. Earlier in the night, Australian star Skye Nicolson easily outpointed Miyo Yoshida to retain the WBC super-bantamweight title, meaning a unification with Ali could ensue. And in the night’s other world-title fight, Irma Garcia beat Nataly Delgado via unanimous decision to keep the IBF super-flyweight belt.
